title: Pennant fleet dispatch edge integration ramble
content:
Context:
- Customer: Pennant Mobility (regional bus operator). Use case: real-time dispatch assistant at edge racks on depots and on-vehicle edge gateways to optimize reroute & ETA messages and handle voice/text operator queries when central connectivity is intermittent.
- Existing stack: dispatch core (Java microservices), fallback rules engine (Lua), telematics over LTE, on-vehicle gateway (NVIDIA Orin NX or TX2-class on older buses), depot edge racks (1x A10G for larger depots).
- Goal for Redwood: provide a private deploy (VPC + on-prem agent) that can run model(s) locally at depot and on a subset of vehicles; consistent API with hosted product but zero calls to public cloud during normal ops.

Meeting notes (2025-02-10 sync):
- Attendees: Leah (Redwood SE), Hiro (Pennant infra), Maya (Pennant ops), Jonas (Redwood runtime), Sasha (Pennant product via audio).
- High-level ask from Pennant: "latency under 200ms for short prompts (intent classification / routing decision), robust offline behavior when LTE drops, cost bounded for 100k events/day per depot."
- They want streaming updates for human operator chat + server-initiated re-routes (low jitter).
- Concern: vehicles are heterogeneous; can't assume GPU on each bus. Strategy: depot-level A10G handles heavy reranks/longer context models, vehicle gateways use smaller quantized models or fall back to local heuristics.

Functional requirements (captured quickly):
- Intents: classify operator commands (short text/voice->transcribed) into ~18 action categories within 95% accuracy target on their prompts.
- Reranking: given candidate route patches (3–5), model should score and prefer minimal added delay and route safety (penalties).
- Context window: need last 6 messages + vehicle telemetry snapshot (~200 tokens) for reasonable answers.
- Streaming: partial token streaming for operator typing and voice transcriptions.
- Audit logs: per-request token counts, model version, latency, and paired telemetry snapshot to support post-mortem.

Nonfunctional / constraints:
- Target P99 latency depot inference: <= 250ms for classification; P50 < 90ms. For vehicle gateway small model: P50 < 150ms when CPU-only (if no GPU), but acceptable to be a bit higher.
- Bandwidth and intermittent connectivity: fallback policy MUST queue requests and perform local deterministic/fallback rules when remote reachability lost >10s.
- Security: no PII leaves vehicle/depot. Keys via on-prem KMS and HSM integration considered.
- Ops: need health-check endpoints, model warmup hooks, and local KV cache eviction policy tied to route frequency.

Technical choreography ideas (brainstorm):
- Model selection: small intent model (distilled 60M–250M) quantized to int8 for vehicle gateways. Depot runs Llama2-style 7B quantized (int8/4-bit) for reranking and contextual completions.
- Cache strategy: prefix caching for common operator sequences ("start detour", "hold at stop"). Warm cache at shift start using last-night snapshot.
- Fallbacks: 1) local rules engine (Lua) as immediate fallback; 2) depot model when vehicle unreachable; 3) precomputed prioritized route table. Automatic degrade: if inference latency > target or CPU contention, return rule-based verdict with annotation.
- KV cache transfer: on reconnect, vehicle sends summary (hashes) so depot can quickly identify missing KV segments to reduce warmup. Consider encrypting cache snapshots.

Gotchas / risks (from their ops team):
- LTE jitter causes spikes in API roundtrips; need circuit breaker and adaptive backoff on streaming.
- Some older buses throttle CPU and kill processes unexpectedly during long routes — must keep agent footprint <200MB resident if possible and avoid swapping.
- Telemetry sampling: high-frequency GPS bursts can bloat audit logs; need sampling rules (e.g., 1Hz when cruising, 5Hz during incidents).
- Model regressions: Pennant will require a canary window (2 weeks) with metrics against baseline on their historical prompt set. Ensure Redwood Optimize can hook into their evals.

Immediate action items / next steps (owner tag):
- Leah: assemble minimal end-to-end prototype plan (depot A10G + vehicle CPU fallback) and send to Pennant by 2025-02-14.
- Jonas: prototype a lightweight intent model conversion pipeline (FP32 -> int8) and test on Orin NX baseline by 2025-02-17.
- Hiro (customer): provide 1 week sample of operator transcripts + anonymized telemetry (drop PII) and list of top 50 operator utterances by frequency. Deadline 2025-02-16.
- Maya: confirm compliance checklist items they need (SOC2/ISO concerns) and whether they require HSM-backed key storage.
- Team: schedule 1-hour on-site depot runbook walkthrough week of 2025-02-24.

Acceptance criteria for MVP (proposal):
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on their holdout set.
- Depot P50 classification latency < 120ms, P95 < 300ms.
- Fallback rule triggered and labeled in 100% of test partitioned network outages over 30s.
- Audit logs captured and retrievable for sample incident within 30 minutes.

Prompt / eval notes (raw):
- Example operator prompts (short): "delay on 42A, reroute via Elm St?" "hold at last stop until ETA updates" "bus 17 needs wheelchair assist, reroute?"
- Sensitive phrases: passenger names, incident descriptions; enforce redaction step in preprocessor.
- Evaluation harness: replay telemetry + prompts, measure metric: action correctness (binary), latency, and fallback incidence.

Operational checklist idea (deployment):
- Pre-deploy: generate offline quantized model, run synthetic latency and memory profile, produce config bundle with warmup sequence and sample cache snapshot.
- On install: agent installs as systemd service, health port 9108, rest endpoint /v1/predict, metrics to local prometheus + pushgateway.
- Monitoring: set alerts if inference error rate >1% or if model load time > 60s after reboot.

Open questions to clarify with Pennant (to add to next agenda):
- Which vehicles will be in-scope for GPU vs CPU-only? Can we get exact hardware inventory?
- Tolerance for silently switching to rule-based fallback vs explicit operator notification. They leaned toward silent fallback but ops wants logging and manual override.
- Are there regulatory retention windows for audit logs (30/90/365 days)?
- Do they require on-prem KMS or will a Redwood-managed key inside their VPC be acceptable?

Loose timeline (proposal sketch):
- Week 1 (now -> 2025-02-21): data ingest + small model conversion + prototype on dev Orin.
- Week 2: depot A10G integration + streaming proof-of-concept + canary harness.
- Week 3: on-prem install dry-run + ops runbook + SLA discussion.

Notes to self (short):
- Keep model size conservative for vehicles. Prioritize correctness for intent classification over flashy completions.
- Add explicit trace IDs in telemetry -> inference logs mapping for postmortem.
- Pitch Redwood Optimize initial suggestions (batching not relevant at vehicle level, but model quantization and cache warmups will buy most wins).

End of scratchpad.
summary: Working sketch for Pennant Mobility edge onramp: intent classification + reranking architecture, latency targets, fallback policies, action items and open questions. Draft for internal alignment before customer walk-through.
